For a **Maven + Spring Boot project**, you should generally ignore generated build files, IDE files, logs, and local environment/config files.

Create a file named **`.gitignore`** in the **root of your project**, at the same level as `pom.xml`.

### Recommended `.gitignore`

```gitignore
# =========================
# Maven
# =========================
target/
!.mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.jar

# Maven generated files
pom.xml.tag
pom.xml.releaseBackup
pom.xml.versionsBackup
pom.xml.next
release.properties
dependency-reduced-pom.xml


# =========================
# IntelliJ IDEA
# =========================
.idea/
*.iml
*.iws
*.ipr


# =========================
# VS Code
# =========================
.vscode/


# =========================
# Eclipse
# =========================
.classpath
.project
.settings/
.factorypath


# =========================
# Java
# =========================
*.class
*.log


# =========================
# OS files
# =========================
.DS_Store
Thumbs.db


# =========================
# Spring Boot / Local Config
# =========================

# Local environment files
.env
.env.*

# Local application configuration
application-local.properties
application-local.yml
application-local.yaml

# Logs
logs/
*.log
```

### Your project should look like

```text
my-spring-project/
│
├── .gitignore
├── pom.xml
├── src/
│   ├── main/
│   │   ├── java/
│   │   └── resources/
│   │       └── application.properties
│   │
│   └── test/
│       └── java/
│
└── target/          ← ignored by Git
```

### Important: Don't ignore these

You **should commit**:

```text
pom.xml
src/
mvnw
mvnw.cmd
.mvn/wrapper/
```

If you generated the project using Spring Initializr and have Maven Wrapper files, keep them in Git. This allows another developer to run:

```cmd
mvnw.cmd spring-boot:run
```

without having Maven globally installed.

### One important Spring Boot rule

Don't blindly ignore `application.properties`.

For example:

```text
src/main/resources/application.properties
```

is normally part of your application and **should be committed**.

But if you have secrets:

```properties
spring.datasource.username=myuser
spring.datasource.password=secret123
```

don't commit those credentials. Prefer environment variables:

```properties
spring.datasource.username=${DB_USERNAME}
spring.datasource.password=${DB_PASSWORD}
```

and keep your local `.env` or local configuration ignored.

### After creating `.gitignore`

Run:

```cmd
git status
```

You should **not** see:

```text
target/
.idea/
*.iml
```

Then:

```cmd
git add .
git commit -m "Initial Spring Boot project"
```

For your **React → Spring Boot transition**, this is a good `.gitignore` setup to use for your first Maven/Spring Boot projects.
